coverageSpotVerification.detail: The manifest covers every suite-required assertion of every in-scope milestone with no gaps (M1 7/7, M2 22/22, M3 7/7, M4 5/5, M5 6/6, M6 5/5, M8 6/6) and pins the same assertions.json SHA-256 the grader verified. 30 of the 58 mappings were read against their test bodies and, where the test is re-runnable, against the grader's own re-execution of the same observable. All 30 mapped tests do exercise the assertion they claim, and no milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure. Three mappings are honest but under-strength and are named here rather than left implicit: (1) m8-a06's test exercises the shared trailing-24 h predicate as a pure function over synthetic rows instead of querying metrics:trending — the substitution is named in the test's own title and is forced by the replay contract's no-backdating rule, since no post in the corpus can be older than 24 hours; (2) m3-a11's jump check asserts only that the original bubble's boundingBox y >= 0 after tapping the excerpt, which a page that never scrolled would also satisfy; (3) m2-a12's link test asserts that a role=link element exists and no iframe does, but not the 'opening the system browser' clause. The grader re-verified all three observables independently and each holds. Two further weaknesses without a coverage consequence: m2-a20's chronological-order clause is exercised with a single reply, and m5-a09's case-insensitivity clause is not asserted by the mapped test.

defects.summary: The documented backend start command cannot deploy functions from a clean checkout: convex/tsconfig.json omits "types": ["node"], so `convex dev` fails its TypeScript gate with six TS2591 'Cannot find name process' errors and refuses to push. The local backend still listens and serves whatever was previously pushed, so the failure is silent to anyone who does not read the log.
defects.evidence: grading/logs/convex-dev.log (grader's own run of the README command, 6 errors in convex/auth.config.ts, convex/digest.ts, convex/media.ts, convex/push.ts); reproduced directly with `tsc -p convex/tsconfig.json` and shown to be exactly this cause because `tsc -p convex/tsconfig.json --types node` exits 0. The lane's own evidence/typecheck*.log files are all 0 bytes because they typecheck the root tsconfig, which includes only app/**/*.tsx and ui/**.

defects.summary: `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m8` fails deterministically once the server UTC day differs from the UTC day of the seeded activity: the mapped test asserts that the previous six day-buckets are all zero, which only holds while every seeded post lies inside the current UTC day. M8's green receipt is therefore not reproducible at an arbitrary wall-clock time.
defects.evidence: grading/logs/grader-m8-acceptance.log — FAIL server-utc-today-and-zero-day-buckets at the final assert.ok in scripts/tests-m8.mjs; the grader's run was at 03:10Z on 2026-09-25 while the seeded corpus was written at 18:00–20:30Z on 2026-09-24. The two assertions the test carries (m8-a03, m8-a04) both pass under independent re-execution (grading/results-api-m8-metrics.json).

defects.summary: The typing indicator's expiry sits exactly on the 5 s bound rather than inside it, so it fails the stated bar in a majority of trials. chat:typing schedules clearTyping 4 500 ms after the typing mutation and chat.detail() additionally treats typing as live while typing > now − 5 000 ms, both measured from the last server-recorded typing event rather than from the last keystroke; a debounced trailing mutation pushes expiry past 5 s after the final keystroke.
defects.evidence: evidence/m3-choreography.jsonl :: typing-indicator-within-2s-expires-within-5s — attempt 1 expiresAfterLastKeystrokeMs 4811.1 (pass); attempts 2 and 3 failed with sm-convo-typing still visible when 5 s waits elapsed at settlementWaitMs 5028.4 and 5037.4. Source: convex/chat.ts typing/clearTyping and chat.ts detail().

defects.summary: The shortened grading configs are hard-wired into the server modules, so the retained production values are unreachable without a code edit: convex/ephemeral.ts and convex/media.ts statically import ../config/windows.shortened.json and convex/digest.ts statically imports ../config/digest.shortened.json. There is no configuration-selection seam, so the claim that production defaults are 'retained alongside' the grading profile is documentation only.
defects.evidence: convex/ephemeral.ts line 7, convex/media.ts line 16, convex/digest.ts line 4; config/windows.production.json and config/digest.production.json are present but referenced nowhere in convex/, app/, components/ or lib/.

defects.summary: A published evidence artifact retains plaintext credentials for lane-generated test accounts. evidence/digest-proof-private.json stores the email and password of three digest personas in clear text inside the evidence directory, against LLP 0197's redaction posture; the fixture pack's declared credential exception covers only the fixture pack's own files.
defects.evidence: evidence/digest-proof-private.json — object keys {stamp, end, setupEpoch, clients, credentials}, with credentials.a/b/c each holding a plaintext password (5 occurrences of the shared password suffix). The companion public evidence/digest-proof.json contains none, so the separation was deliberate; the private file is still retained in the published tree.

defects.summary: People search is a full-table scan per query while message search is indexed. chat:people collects every profiles row and filters candidates in JavaScript, so its cost grows linearly with the account count on every keystroke, in contrast to ephemeral:search which uses the p1/p2/p3 prefix indexes. Correct and fast at the brief's ~1 000-user envelope, but the only read path in the app with no index behind it.
defects.evidence: convex/chat.ts people query (ctx.db.query("profiles").withIndex("by_creation_time", ...).collect() followed by an in-JS filter); measured correct at the scale instance's 1 008 profiles, and the grader's scale probes show no rule violation.

defects.summary: Cold-start initial sync of the 100-conversation probe user needs one round trip per conversation: chat:list returns the conversations but every first page of history is a separate chat:history call, and chat:list itself re-joins every member's profile for every conversation on every call. At the scale envelope the grader measured 24.3 s of sequential wall time for the 100-conversation cold sync under machine load (1.0 s on a quiet machine), 555 KiB transferred.
defects.evidence: grading/scale-probes-final.json initialSync {conversations 100, histories 100, wallMs 24333, responseBytes 568 419, rssGrowthBytes 838 656}; convex/chat.ts list() -> detail() per row. The degradation rule only requires no timeout and no unbounded memory growth, both of which hold.

defects.summary: User-facing error surfaces render raw Convex server-error envelopes rather than the message. The duplicate-handle path puts the full transport envelope — function name, request id, 'Uncaught ConvexError', source file and line number, 'Called by client' — into sm-profile-error, leaking internal paths into the UI. The visible-error bar is met; the presentation is not product quality.

O1.anchorsCited: Interpolated between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), with every milestone of the full run's scope in the denominator regardless of status.
O1.justification: 104 of the 119 in-scope assertions pass under independent grader execution. M1-M5 are complete and green with every assertion re-verified by the grader (API, source inspection and browser automation), well past the 60 anchor. The 90 anchor fails on both of its explicit conditions. First, platform-proof artifacts do not exist: evidence/m6-choreography.jsonl and evidence/m8-choreography.jsonl record ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as 'not-recorded', so m6-a01..a04 and m8-a17..a18 (6 assertions) have no evidence on their named surface. Second, M7 was not attempted at all under instrument/ENVIRONMENT.md's ordering, and its 9 assertions score not passed. Of what was attempted, quality is high rather than merely nominally green: the grader's re-execution found no failing assertion, no wrong data, and no authorization hole across the full checklist plus a dozen additional trust-boundary probes. Placement at 78 reflects 87.4 % of the frozen checklist passing at grader strength with the native-proof leg entirely absent.

O2.anchorsCited: Interpolated between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'); defects are severity-weighted, where MATERIAL means blocker or major.
O2.justification: Nine defects beyond the checklist: 0 blocker, 2 major, 5 minor, 2 cosmetic. Both majors are reproducibility defects in the lane's own documented gates rather than product misbehaviour — d-01, where convex/tsconfig.json's missing "types": ["node"] makes the documented `convex dev` command fail its typecheck and silently refuse to push functions, and d-02, where the M8 acceptance test's assumption that the previous six UTC day-buckets are empty makes `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m8` fail deterministically once the UTC day rolls over. That is materially better than the 60 anchor: across roughly sixty independent checks, including cross-user DM reads, non-member and token-less asset fetches, view-once re-fetch, post-window edit and delete, post-logout token reuse, push-log and search scoping and scheduled-digest membership isolation, the grader found zero data-correctness and zero authorization defects, and every server-side denial was correct. It is short of the 90 anchor because two majors block reproducing the lane's own green bar and because the minors are real product-surface issues (d-03's typing-expiry boundary failing 2 of 3 trials, d-04's hard-wired grading configs, d-05's plaintext credentials retained in published evidence).

O4.anchorsCited: Below the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app'), against a dimension defined as 'what the offline acceptance actually demonstrated, and honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee'.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's mechanically checkable simulator artifacts, as applicability.json requires. There are none: evidence/m6-choreography.jsonl records supplementalExternal ios-simulator-m6 with status 'not-recorded' and pass null, and evidence/m8-choreography.jsonl records ios-simulator-m8 the same way, so M8's durable-queue-restart and multi-device native evidence is absent too. Nothing was demonstrated about native cold-start offline behaviour: not history rendering, not previously viewed media, not offline search, and not the view-once non-persistence check. That places the demonstration axis below the 30 anchor, which still presumes the native proof ran and showed something. The score is not lower because the dimension's second scored component is the honesty of the gap, and this lane discharges it exactly: README.md states that artifacts/mN-ios are Hermes build artifacts and not simulator proofs and that evidence/offline-restart-proof.json is a browser restart proof and not an iOS claim, and the harness receipts carry an explicit 'not-recorded' status with a reason rather than a fabricated pass. Note for the record, not as O4 credit: the equivalent behaviours do hold on the web build — evidence/m6-choreography.jsonl's offline-message-queue-flush-in-order and m8-a15/a16 pass, and evidence/offline-restart-proof.json documents a genuine cold browser relaunch with a durable pending queue, cold offline search and a receipt reaching read.

O5.bandRationale: First-match evaluation in the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: the grader independently verified that all 18 per-entity counts in invariant-manifest-combined.json match the replayed instance exactly and that every named O5 fixture is exact through the public authenticated API (u0500 following 500 / conversations 100, u0005 following 5, u0900 followers 900 and 200 top-level posts, u0901 following exactly {u0001,u0002,u0003,u0004,u0900}, g0001 50 members and 10 000 messages counted by full paging over 200 pages), and the replay completed on its own recorded clock in 5 281.8 s (88.0 min) with 167 243 actions settled, so no wall cap was exhausted. Band 30 does not fire: the grader re-measured every published degradation rule on the scale instance at k=20 after 3 warm-ups, sequential, 30 s timeout, and all pass with no probe timing out, erroring or OOMing — deep paging page 50 / page 1 = 0.99x, 500-follow / 5-follow Following feed = 1.06x, celebrity-follower / 5-follow read path = 1.27x, 50-member group send / 2-member DM send = 1.17x (1.17x again on a third run), celebrity / 5-follower post-create ack = 1.14x on the first run and 2.81-2.84x on two later runs under heavier load, all inside the 3x bound; Insights returns a 584-byte payload independent of corpus size, so it does not transfer the corpus to the client; the 100-conversation cold sync completed with bounded memory. Band 60 does not fire: no absolute p95 ceiling is exceeded because the instrument's ceiling table is still the unpopulated P3 placeholder, and the replay's 88.0 min is 36.7 % of the only numeric wall bound available in this run (instrument/ENVIRONMENT.md's four-hour per-milestone safety limit), not more than 80 %. Band 90 cannot be established: it requires every probe's observed ceiling utilization to be <= 50 %, and with no calibrated absolute ceilings frozen, ceiling utilization is undefined rather than demonstrably low. First-match therefore falls through to 75.

notes: probeResults is empty by wave deviation, not by omission: no holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so wave.probeSetSha256 records the string none-uncommitted and execution-order phase 4 was skipped entirely. No probes were invented. O3 is consequently null: applicability.json restricts O3 evidence to the wave's secret rotated holdout probes and rules that anchor probes never bear on it, so with zero scored probes in existence there is no admissible evidence and a number would be fabricated. The grader's own trust-boundary observations (recorded in the assertion results and in trace.md) are deliberately not converted into an O3 score. Under the manifest's nullDimensionRule a null dimension bars any overall weighted total for this run. Second deviation: the claude family has not passed the grader calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false and this grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false because the lane's builder is not known to this session and no abort-fallback regrade occurred. Third deviation: timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3 and machine load (uptime) is recorded beside every timing record in trace.md, because two other lanes shared this host throughout; one-minute load averages ranged from 11.9 to 35.3 during grading. grader.rerunsUsed is 1: the grader's first scale performance-probe pass had a grader-tooling fault (a DM chosen for the 2-member send baseline that the acting user was not a member of, producing 23 'Not a member' errors, and read probes scheduled after the write probes so a pending fan-out backlog inflated read p95s). Per the grader-abort protocol that is a grader-environment failure, not a lane defect; the phase was re-run once with reads before writes and a correct chat and passed cleanly with zero errors and zero timeouts, and a third write-path run confirmed it. The lane shipped no run-record.json, so milestone statuses were not read from a record: they are inferred from the harness's segment summaries, all of which report green:true with nonGreenCause null for m1-m6 and m8. Scope note: the frozen grader-report schema admits only the 101 M1-M7 assertion IDs, so the 18 M8 results required by this wave's complete grade are written to grading/m8-assertion-results.json in the same result-record shape; the two files partition the manifest's 119 unique ids with no overlap. No weighted total, efficiency statistic or cross-lane comparison is computed or reported here.
